items.name: capability
items.description: Frontier capability relevant to catastrophic pathways: autonomy horizon, coding, computer use, cyber and biological uplift, research automation.

signals.name: 50% task-completion time horizon
signals.description: METR-style human task length completed with 50% success by the best published model.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: SWE-bench Verified top score
signals.description: Best tracked percentage of resolved tasks.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: OSWorld-Verified top score
signals.description: Best tracked success rate on real-computer tasks.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Cyber offensive capability
signals.description: Degree to which frontier systems can execute intrusion life-cycle stages autonomously.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = no uplift, 0.5 = autonomous execution of most tactical stages with human strategic control (documented), 1 = fully autonomous campaigns against defended targets

signals.name: Biological/chemical uplift
signals.description: Category-level assessment of uplift for dangerous laboratory work as reported by synthesis reports and developer frameworks; no operational detail.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = no uplift beyond public sources, 0.5 = meaningful assistance with substantial uncertainty about real-world uplift, 1 = expert-level end-to-end uplift established

signals.name: AI research automation
signals.description: Share of AI R&D workflow that frontier systems perform autonomously.

items.name: autonomy
items.description: Reliable unattended operation: task length, self-correction, delegation, persistence.

signals.name: Unattended operation length
signals.description: Longest human-equivalent task length completed reliably by deployed agents.
signals.normalization: clamp(log2(1 + hours) / log2(1 + 168), 0, 1): one work-week of unattended operation → 1
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Evidence of unsanctioned autonomous action
signals.description: Documented cases of agents acting outside sanctioned scope in real environments.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = none documented, 0.5 = contained cases with no real-world harm, 1 = uncontained cases with real-world harm

signals.name: Delegation depth in deployed harnesses
signals.description: Typical nesting depth of agent-to-agent delegation in production systems.

signals.name: Human approval frequency
signals.description: Share of high-impact actions gated by human approval in typical deployments (inverted).
signals.normalization: share of high-impact actions approved by a human, 0–1

items.name: access_exposure
items.description: What deployed systems can reach: tools, credentials, money, code execution, infrastructure, weights.

signals.name: Breadth of tool and credential access
signals.description: Typical scope of tools, credentials and network access granted to deployed agents.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = read-only sandboxed, 0.5 = broad developer-level access common, 1 = production and financial write access common without gates

signals.name: Open-weight proximity to frontier
signals.description: How close the best open-weight models are to the closed frontier.

signals.name: Critical-infrastructure integration
signals.description: Extent of agent integration into operational technology.

items.name: scalability
items.description: How fast capability can be replicated and scaled: compute growth, inference cost, agent population.

signals.name: Frontier training compute growth
signals.description: Annual growth factor of frontier training compute.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Inference cost decline
signals.description: Annual decline factor in the cost of frontier-level inference.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Deployed agent population
signals.description: Order of magnitude of concurrently deployed autonomous agents.

items.name: alignment_control
items.description: Evidence about honesty, corrigibility, shutdown compliance, control evaluations and interpretability.

signals.name: Control-evaluation maturity
signals.description: Whether frontier deployments pass control evaluations at scale.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = none, 0.5 = published protocols with limited deployment use, 1 = routine passing control evaluations for frontier agents

signals.name: Shutdown compliance
signals.description: Evidence that frontier models comply with shutdown and do not sabotage oversight in tests.
signals.normalization: 1 − (severity of documented non-compliance): 1 = consistent compliance, 0.5 = non-compliance in a minority of controlled runs, 0 = routine subversion

signals.name: Interpretability-based deception detection
signals.description: Availability of deployed detectors for deceptive cognition.

signals.name: Alignment-faking evidence
signals.description: Whether model organisms show alignment faking that persists through training (inverted control signal).
signals.normalization: 1 − strength of evidence for persistent alignment faking

items.name: security
items.description: Model-weight security, agent-infrastructure security, supply-chain integrity, prompt-injection resistance.

signals.name: Model-weight security level
signals.description: Best documented security level (RAND SL1–SL5) achieved by frontier developers.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Agent supply-chain integrity
signals.description: Signing, provenance and vulnerability posture of agent tool registries and servers.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = unverified ecosystem with active CVE waves, 0.5 = identity verification without code signing, 1 = signed, scanned, monitored

signals.name: Prompt-injection resistance
signals.description: Degree to which deployed agents resist instruction injection through content and tool metadata.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = routinely exploitable, 0.5 = mitigations common but bypassable, 1 = deterministic isolation standard

signals.name: Cancellation and audit completeness
signals.description: Whether deployed agent stacks support reliable cancellation and complete audit.

items.name: governance
items.description: Binding rules, incident reporting, evaluation capacity, safety frameworks, enforcement, international coordination.

signals.name: Jurisdictions with binding frontier-model rules
signals.description: Count of jurisdictions with binding statutes specifically covering frontier or general-purpose models with systemic risk.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Incident-reporting mandates
signals.description: Coverage of mandatory serious-incident reporting for frontier developers.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = none, 0.5 = mandates in some major jurisdictions with enforcement pending, 1 = global interoperable mandates enforced

signals.name: Third-party evaluation capacity
signals.description: Capacity of independent and government evaluators to test frontier systems pre-deployment.
signals.normalization: judgment scale: 0 = none, 0.5 = government institutes with published tooling and partial access, 1 = mandatory independent pre-deployment evaluation

signals.name: Published frontier safety frameworks
signals.description: Share of the five largest frontier developers with a published, versioned frontier safety framework.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

signals.name: Enforcement active
signals.description: Whether regulators have exercised enforcement powers for frontier-model obligations.

items.name: incidents
items.description: Verified incidents and near misses; computed from incidents.json by the incident pressure index rather than from signals.

signals.name: Verified loss-of-control precursors
signals.description: Count of verified incidents with relevance strong or direct_precursor in the last 24 months.
signals.observation_vs_judgment: observation when a published measurement exists; judgment when qualitative evidence is mapped to the scale

items.name: race_dynamics
items.description: Competitive pressure to deploy before safeguards are ready.

signals.name: Release cadence pressure
signals.description: Frequency of frontier releases and shortening of evaluation windows.

signals.name: Safety commitment erosion
signals.description: Documented weakening of safety commitments or institutions under competitive pressure.

signals.name: Geopolitical competition intensity
signals.description: Degree to which frontier AI is framed and funded as a strategic race between states.

items.name: resilience
items.description: Capacity to absorb and recover from failures: fallbacks, segmentation, emergency governance, distributed expertise.

signals.name: Manual fallback coverage
signals.description: Share of critical services with tested manual fallback.

signals.name: AI emergency-response capacity
signals.description: Existence and exercise of cross-sector AI incident response.

signals.name: Infrastructure diversity
signals.description: Diversity of model and cloud providers behind critical services (inverse monoculture).
